title: Diamondbacks’ Corbin Burnes returns from Tommy John surgery, pitches 3 scoreless innings
content:
At long last, Corbin Burnes has returned to a big-league mound, and for the still-in-the-hunt Arizona Diamondbacks, the timing could not be any better. The former National League Cy Young Award winner last pitched in June 2025 before Tommy John surgery ended his season just months after signing a six-year, $210 million deal with Arizona.

Not yet fully built up, Burnes tossed three scoreless innings Tuesday night against the Kansas City Royals, in his first big-league start in over 450 days. Flashing his signature cutter, Burnes topped out at 94.9 mph on 57 pitches (35 strikes). Burnes struck out two, walked two and allowed two hits over his three frames.

He was replaced in the fourth inning by Kade Strowd, whom the Diamondbacks recalled from Triple A on Tuesday as part of a series of roster moves.

An All-Star and Cy Young Award vote-getter in four straight seasons, Burnes arrived in the desert as one of baseball’s most reliable pitchers, having averaged 31 starts per season between 2021 and 2024. His signing with the Diamondbacks was, in part, driven by his desire to remain in Arizona, where he resided in the offseason. The pact also represented the rare big-money move for a club that entered Tuesday with a payroll that ranked 14th, per Cot’s Baseball Contracts.

However, his time was not for long.

After 11 starts (64 1/3 innings) with a 2.66 ERA, Burnes went down with right elbow inflammation after he exited his final outing, a home game against the Washington Nationals, midway through the fifth inning. The then-30-year-old opted to undergo elbow surgery, ending his 2025 season and putting him out for part of 2026.

“Corbin made this decision,” manager Torey Lovullo said at the time. “He’s got a team of unbelievable people around him. … Everybody was weighing in on what was going on. Listening to what the potential plan could be, whether it was conservative or having (Tommy John surgery). Corbin got all that information, lumped it up and made his own decision on this. We’re going to support him.”

Were it not for a right teres major muscle strain, Burnes would have returned to the Diamondbacks’ rotation sooner. However, a setback in June during his rehab process pushed his return from after the All-Star break into September.

On Aug. 29, Burnes took the biggest step in his return to play, appearing in a minor-league rehab game. That, plus a bridge camp game when he tossed 50-plus pitches, gave Arizona enough confidence to entrust Burnes with returning to its rotation.

“I think it’s been more probably the last two, 2 1/2 months that it’s really been challenging,” Burnes told MLB.com. “Part of this, we’ve been going at it for a year and a half now without any breaks. So when we got the news that it was gonna be a little longer, I think it was initially tough, and then you start getting back into it, and you kind of start seeing the light at the end of the tunnel, which is good, but it’s been tough.”

The Diamondbacks, who entered Tuesday’s contest in possession of the NL’s third and final wild-card spot, have seen several players return over the past few weeks. On Aug. 31, the club activated Ketel Marte from the 10-day injured list, ending a two-week saga that saw the second baseman also placed on the restricted list after no-showing the series opener at Fenway Park.

Separately, Arizona also returned Lourdes Gurriel Jr. to its lineup, along with reliever Justin Martinez, who also had Tommy John surgery. The club still expects to return starters Ryne Nelson, Zac Gallen and Michael Soroka. Their impending returns, plus Burnes, should help fortify the Diamondbacks’ rotation and bullpen, depending on how Arizona wants to deploy its pitchers.

Suddenly, what was once a weakness for the Diamondbacks could immediately turn into a massive strength. The club also has Eduardo Rodríguez (2026 All-Star, 2.55 ERA) and Brandon Pfaadt (2.41 ERA over his last eight starts).

Entering Tuesday, FanGraphs estimated the Diamondbacks’ playoff odds at 55.2 percent. The club wraps up its three-game set against the Royals on Wednesday before returning home for a nine-game stand against the Texas Rangers, Miami Marlins and New York Yankees. The Diamondbacks close the regular season on the road against the Colorado Rockies and San Diego Padres.

Of that group, the Yankees and Padres were the only two clubs to have records above .500 entering play Tuesday. Arizona, which made the World Series in 2023, has not returned to the postseason since then.
